Can you provide information about your controller (brand, model, etc.) and GUID?

I think I've just encountered this same issue (Godot 3.6, Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS) and wanted to share some additional context from my own experience.

My 8BitDo Ultimate 2C had a number of mapping issues.  The one I noticed the most was that the left trigger seemed to be mapped to the right joystick axis, so after pressing LT once, the right joystick input appeared to be held to the left (it seems like the same thing happened in the video above as well).  That GUID was in the [SDL_GameControllerDB](https://github.com/mdqinc/SDL_GameControllerDB) gamecontrollerdb.txt, so after writing a script to read that file in everything was working well.

However, more recently, I was trying to get an EasySMX ESM-9100 working and it seemed to have the same issues, despite loading in all the mappings from the updated gamecontrollerdb.txt, because it wasn't present in the file. Using the Joypads project to remap the controller worked, so I submitted [this pull request](https://github.com/mdqinc/SDL_GameControllerDB/pull/823) today.  However, that was quickly closed with the suggestion that this could a be a Godot issue.

> B: ABS=3003f
> B: FF=107030000 0
> ```

Judging from the name, this seems to be a game controller, but it still needs to be judged based on fields such as "H: Handlers" (`js0`) and "B: KEY". 

You can install `evemu-tools`/`evtest`, and then use `evemu-record`/`evtest` to parse in the terminal. The following explains how it is parsed:

The "B:" field is the bit flag field, and the index counts from right to left, starting from 0.
So, according to the `B: KEY` field, the key events **supported** by EasySMX ESM-9100 (030000005e0400008e02000078010000) are:
```
# 0x7cdb = 0b0111110011011011
be0 = 4*(4*16) + 4*12 = 304 (0x130 BTN_SOUTH)
be1 = 305 BTN_EAST
be2 = 307 BTN_NORTH
be3 = 308 BTN_WEST
be4 = 310 BTN_TL
be5 = 311 BTN_TR
be6 = 314  BTN_SELECT
be7 = 315  BTN_START
be8 = 316 BTN_MODE
be9 = 317 BTN_THUMBL
be10 = 318 BTN_THUMBR
```
Base on https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/3d3a9c8b89d4f8a3785e06ffd15405c670696f02/include/uapi/linux/input-event-codes.h#L380-L399. Because the button event `BTN_SOUTH` is supported, the device is recognized by Linux as a Gamepad (see https://docs.kernel.org/input/gamepad.html#detection).

Other types of fields are parsed following similar steps. `evemu-tools`/`evtest` provides commands that can display parsing results.


For newer devices that support the `BTN_SOUTH` event you can try #95486.

```
I: Bus=0003 Vendor=045e Product=028e Version=0178
N: Name="Microsoft X-Box 360 pad"
```

This is actually a case of third-party vendors using the Xbox mapping scheme. If this is the case, I would not recommend adding a mapping record to the upstream [SDL_GameControllerDB](https://github.com/mdqinc/SDL_GameControllerDB) unless you are certain that such a mapping actually exists for the Xbox.

I've updated the proc info with the additional entries that were found for the 8BitDo controller.

Also, yes, I did change the name for the mapping, it is actually identified as "Microsoft X-Box 360 pad."  There was a note in the README about making sure the name was relevant so I assumed that was potentially expected.  Sorry for the confusion!
